small_guidance: The conv kernel is the bottleneck (97% time, fast_p=0.20). Currently each program loops over IC and all KD*KH*KW positions doing scalar w_val[:, None] * x_val[None, :] outer products which underutilizes tensor cores. Restructure as a real GEMM: gather an im2col tile of shape (BLOCK_K, BLOCK_SPATIAL) where K = IC*KD*KH*KW (or a chunk), and a weight tile (BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_K), then use tl.dot for the accumulation. Try (BLOCK_OC=64, BLOCK_SPATIAL=64, BLOCK_K=32) num_warps=4 num_stages=2, and add (32,128,32) and (64,32,32) variants. Also reduce register pressure (currently 100 reg/thread, occupancy 16.7%) by chunking IC inside one loop rather than fully unrolling KD*KH*KW.
large_guidance: Rewrite the ConvTranspose3d as a gather-style GEMM mapping each output voxel to an inner product over (IC, KD, KH, KW) with tl.dot. One program handles a (BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_SPATIAL) output tile; inside, loop over the K dimension in BLOCK_K chunks, computing source input indices (od+PD-kd)/SD with validity masks, loading a (BLOCK_K, BLOCK_SPATIAL) input panel and (BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_K) weight panel, then `acc += tl.dot(w_tile, x_tile)`. This converts the current scalar outer-product loop into tensor-core MMA and should cut the 9.5ms conv time substantially. Additionally, fuse the BatchNorm (eval-folded scale/shift using running stats and affine params) and the spatial mean-subtract into a single epilogue pass, replacing both cuDNN BN and the separate fused_meansub kernel — though those are <1% and secondary. Use channels-last-style indexing so the spatial axis is contiguous for coalesced loads.
